collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A family's garden was taken unfairly long ago, but others have farmed it for decades: share it, or offer other repair.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has learned from an old elder that the garden on the sunny slope belonged to (subject.his/her) family, until it was taken generations ago in an unfair trade. For forty years, (friend)'s family has farmed it, and it is the only garden they have ever known. Neither family did anything wrong. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The two families agree to farm the slope together. It is awkward at first: two ways of planting, two ways of weeding. By the third season, the children of both families are running between the rows as if it had always been one garden.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village gives (subject)'s family a new garden on the hill and carves their old family mark on a stone at the edge of the sunny slope. (subject) is grateful, and also not satisfied. Some things cannot be fully repaired. The stone stays.
